text: The 3-dimensional vectors $$ \wvec_1 = \threevec1{-1}1,\hspace{24pt} \wvec_2 = \threevec1{1}0,\hspace{24pt} \wvec_3 = \threevec1{-1}{-2}. $$ form an orthogonal set, which can be verified by computing $$ \begin{array}{rcl} \wvec_1\cdot\wvec_2 \amp {}={} \amp 0 \\ \wvec_1\cdot\wvec_3 \amp {}={} \amp 0 \\ \wvec_2\cdot\wvec_3 \amp {}={} \amp 0\text{.} \\ \end{array} $$ Notice that this set of vectors forms a basis for $\real^3$.
